title: Grothendieck–Lefschetz formula over $\Qlb$
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$p,a,q,k_0,k$, where $q=p^a$, and the
coefficient conventions.
Let $X_0$ be a
separated finite-type
$k_0$-scheme, put $X=X_0\times_{k_0}k$, let
$K\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,\Qlb)$ be a
Weil complex, represented by
$(E,K_E)$ with $E/\Ql$ finite in $\Qlb$ and
$K_E\in D^b_{c,\mathrm W}(X,E)$, as in the
common-stage
coefficient construction, with underlying Weil map
$\varphi_E:Lg_\gamma^*K_E\to K_E$ in $D^b_c(X,E)$. The Frobenius operators
$F^{\,m}_{c,K}$ on $R\Gamma_c(X,K)=R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)\otimes_E\Qlb$ and
$F_{y,m}$ on $K_{\bar y}=K_{E,\bar y}\otimes_E\Qlb$ are the scalar
extensions of the $E$-stage operators of $(K_E,\varphi_E)$ of
[prop-trf-rational-frobenius-integral-model]; at the finite levels these
are the operators of [def-trf-frobenius-operators]. No integral Weil
presentation of $\varphi_E$, or of any rescaling of it, is assumed.
Assume only the finite-level hypotheses of [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] for
some lattice of $K_E$: at every level $A_{E,n}$, an explicit etale-origin
witness for its reduction and compactification admissibility.
For every integer $m\geq1$,

$$
\boxed{
\sum_{i\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^i
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{c,K}^{\,m}\mid H_c^i(X,K)\bigr)
=
\sum_{y\in X_0(\mathbf F_{q^m})}
\sum_{j\in\mathbf Z}(-1)^j
\operatorname{Tr}\bigl(F_{y,m}\mid H^j(K_{\bar y})\bigr).}
$$

All vector spaces are finite-dimensional over $\Qlb$, only finitely
many degrees occur, every trace is the image of an $E$-valued trace
along $E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$, and the equality is independent of the
finite field, the representative, and the common overfield.

proof.text: Apply [thm-trf-trace-formula-e] to the represented finite-stage pair $(E,K_E)$ and its morphism $\varphi_E$. That theorem gives finite-dimensional $E$-cohomology in only finitely many degrees and the trace identity in $E$ for the $E$-stage Frobenius operators. By the supertrace-over-a-field clause of [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], each categorical trace in that identity is the alternating sum of the ordinary traces on the corresponding cohomology groups.

source.place: first sentence through the supertrace-law sentence

proof.text: The displayed scalar-extension identifications in the statement apply to $P=R\Gamma_c(X,K_E)$ with $v=F_{c,K_E}^{\,m}$ and to $P=K_{E,\bar y}$ with $v=F_{y,m}$. Put $\rho:E\hookrightarrow\Qlb$. Since every short exact sequence of $E$-vector spaces splits, tensoring with $\Qlb$ preserves kernels, images and their quotients; hence $H^r(P\otimes_E\Qlb)=H^r(P)\otimes_E\Qlb$, with induced operator $H^r(v)\otimes_E1$. An $E$-basis of $H^r(P)$ becomes a $\Qlb$-basis after extension, and the matrix of the induced operator is obtained by applying $\rho$ entrywise. Thus the dimension and the vanishing degrees are preserved, and its ordinary trace is $\sum_b\rho(M_{bb})=\rho(\sum_b M_{bb})$, the image of the individual $E$-trace. This proves the finiteness and individual-trace assertions. For the categorical interpretation, [def-trf-karoubi-trace] with $e=1$ gives $\operatorname{tr}_E(v\circ1\mid P)=\operatorname{tr}_E(v\mid P)$; its scalar extension is the categorical trace over $\Qlb$ by [prop-trf-trace-formal-laws], and the supertrace clause of that proposition identifies it with the alternating cohomological trace over $\Qlb$. Applying the additive map $\rho$ to the finite sums in the $E$-identity of Step 1 therefore gives exactly the boxed identity.

source.place: The object K is represented by K_E ... hence applying the summand trace ...

proof.text: Let $(F,L_F,\varphi_F)$ be another finite-stage representative of the same Weil complex $(K,\varphi)$ over $\Qlb$, so that the compared Frobenius endomorphisms are compatible. By [prop-trf-karoubi-independence], after passage to a common finite coefficient overfield the two transported objects are isomorphic and the compatible Frobenius endomorphisms and their iterates have equal summand traces; its comparisons are transitive. Applying this assertion to the global and stalk operators in the trace identity proves independence of the finite coefficient field of definition and of the representative. Transitivity compares the two choices of common overfield after passing to a further common finite overfield, so the resulting $\Qlb$-valued identity is independent of that choice as well.
